title: Supporting safer, smoother travel across Georgia
summary: As transportation demands grow across metropolitan Atlanta, Jacobs will deliver roadway, bridge and safety improvements that keep people and goods moving. Discover how data-driven insights and construction expertise are supporting one of Georgia’s busiest transportation corridors.
body_markdown:
Reliable transportation networks are essential to


growth


and connectivity. As metropolitan Atlanta continues to grow, maintaining mobility while delivering critical infrastructure improvements is essential to travelers.


Georgia Department of Transportation (GDOT) selected Jacobs to provide construction engineering and inspection services for transportation improvements


along the I-285 corridor serving Fulton and Cobb counties


in District 7. The project will advance roadway, bridge and safety improvements that strengthen mobility across one of Georgia’s most heavily traveled regions.


### **Keeping travelers moving during construction**


Delivering major transportation improvements while minimizing disruption is a challenge in busy transportation corridors.


Drawing on


more than two decades of experience supporting GDOT programs, Jacobs will keep projects moving safely and efficiently while reducing impacts on local communities. Through construction oversight, quality


management


and coordination across project teams, Jacobs will support the successful delivery of critical transportation investments.


“Reliable transportation networks are essential to thriving communities,” says Jacobs Project Manager Jeremy Scott. “We’re proud to support improvements that enhance safety, strengthen mobility and keep communities connected throughout construction.”


### **Using data to improve mobility and safety**


Jacobs will


leverage its data-driven traffic analysis capabilities utilizing


[StreetLight](https://www.jacobs.com/solutions/streetlight) to optimize construction staging, lane closures and detour routes throughout project delivery. Combining real-time traffic data with decades of field experience, the team will make informed decisions that improve safety and maintain mobility.


This approach will enable the team to better understand travel patterns, reducing congestion


impacts


and supporting efficient construction operations across one of the region’s busiest transportation corridors.


### **Building resilience for the future**


The program promotes infrastructure resilience through environmental stewardship and responsible construction practices. Jacobs brings extensive experience managing stormwater requirements and erosion control measures as well as environmental compliance on complex transportation projects.


From improving safety to reducing congestion and supporting economic growth, transportation investments along the I-285 corridor will benefit communities across the Atlanta region.
